title: Summarize in exactly 3 bullets
prompt: Summarize the following documentation excerpt in exactly 3 bullet points (use "- " as bullet marker). Maximum 80 words in total. Output only the bullets.
context:
C. Congressional District and ZIP Code Matching Procedures
SOI uses a commercial file to match ZIP codes to congressional districts. The matching process first utilizes the 9-digit ZIP code, if present on the return, to determine the proper congressional district for that return. Nearly 97 percent of the returns match on the 9-digit ZIP code. When the 9-digit ZIP code is not available, the matching process uses the 5-digit ZIP code to determine the proper congressional district. Returns that do not match on ZIP code, or where a ZIP code is not present, are excluded from the data.
Eight states (AK, DC, DE, MT, ND, SD, VT, and WY) have only one congressional district, therefore the matching procedures are not performed on these states. Returns with only one congressional district represent 2 percent of the total number of returns.
reference:
- ZIP codes are matched to congressional districts with a commercial file, using the 9-digit ZIP first (≈97% of returns match) and the 5-digit ZIP as fallback.
- Returns without a matching or present ZIP code are excluded.
- Eight single-district states (AK, DC, DE, MT, ND, SD, VT, WY) skip matching; they are 2% of returns.

title: Multi-step arithmetic reasoning
prompt: A congressional district has 412,000 tax returns. 97% of them match on the 9-digit ZIP code. Of the remaining returns, 80% match on the 5-digit ZIP code. All returns that still do not match are excluded. How many returns are excluded? Explain your reasoning briefly, then give the final answer on the last line as: Answer: <number>
reference: 412,000 × 3% = 12,360 not matched on 9-digit ZIP; 20% of 12,360 = 2,472 excluded. Answer: 2472

title: Rewrite for a non-expert
prompt: Rewrite the following text in plain language for someone with no tax knowledge. Keep every rule, but explain any acronym. Maximum 120 words.
context: SOI did not attempt to correct any ZIP codes listed on the tax returns; however, it did take the following precautions to avoid disclosing information about specific taxpayers: Income and tax items with less than 20 returns for a particular AGI class were combined with another AGI class within the same congressional district. Collapsed AGI classes are identified with a double asterisk (**) in the Excel files. Income and tax items with less than 20 returns for a congressional district were excluded.
reference: Must keep: ZIP codes were not corrected; groups with fewer than 20 returns in an income bracket are merged with another bracket (marked ** in the Excel files); items with fewer than 20 returns in a district are dropped; the purpose is protecting taxpayer privacy. AGI = Adjusted Gross Income, SOI = Statistics of Income.

title: Mermaid flowchart of a procedure
prompt: Draw the procedure below as a Mermaid flowchart. Requirements: start with "flowchart TD"; put the preparation steps (waiting and gathering the three items) inside a subgraph titled "Prepare" and the steps in the online tool inside a subgraph titled "Check status"; draw every decision as a diamond whose outgoing edges are labelled (for example yes / no); show the loop back when the entered data does not match; use between 12 and 25 nodes; put any label that contains parentheses or quotes inside double quotes. Output only one ```mermaid code block, with no explanation.
context:
Checking the status of a federal tax refund

When to start: if the return was filed electronically, wait 24 hours before checking; if it was mailed on paper, wait 4 weeks.
What to gather: the Social Security number (or ITIN), the filing status, and the exact whole-dollar refund amount shown on the return.
How to check: open the online tool and enter the three items. If they do not match the return on file, the tool shows an error: verify the items and enter them again. If they match, the tool shows one of three statuses: Return Received, Refund Approved or Refund Sent.
- Return Received: the return is being processed; check again the next day (the tool is updated once a day, usually overnight).
- Refund Approved: the tool shows the date the refund will be sent.
- Refund Sent: with direct deposit, allow up to 5 days for the bank to post the money; with a paper check, allow several weeks for delivery by mail.
When to call: only if the tool tells you to, or if more than 21 days have passed since e-filing (6 weeks since mailing a paper return) without a Refund Approved status.
reference: One valid "flowchart TD" in a single ```mermaid block, nothing else. Subgraph "Prepare": a decision on how the return was filed (e-filed -> wait 24 hours; paper -> wait 4 weeks) and gathering SSN/ITIN, filing status and the exact refund amount. Subgraph "Check status": enter the three items -> decision "data matches?" whose "no" edge loops back to re-entering the data; a status decision with three branches Return Received / Refund Approved / Refund Sent; Return Received -> check again the next day; Refund Approved -> date the refund will be sent; Refund Sent -> decision direct deposit (up to 5 days) vs paper check (several weeks). The call rule (only if the tool says so, or more than 21 days after e-filing / 6 weeks after mailing without Refund Approved) appears as a decision or a clearly labelled node. Every decision edge is labelled. No invented steps, numbers or statuses.
